src/retry.rs.what: Calls the bank again when a call fails for a reason that passes: at most six tries, each wait longer than the last and at a random point.
src/retry.rs.change: It used to wait half a second, three tries at most. Now each wait may double, to 30 seconds, at a random point, six tries at most.

parts.says: Runs `call`, and after a failure that may pass, waits and tries again; a failure a retry can’t fix comes back at once, as [[Transient errors]] do.
parts.before: Waited a fixed half second between tries.

parts.says: The longest the next wait may be: 200 milliseconds, doubled for each try so far, never past 30 seconds. That is [[Exponential backoff]].
**Waits a random time below that ceiling, so callers that failed together don’t all come back at once.** That is [[Jitter]].
The first wait is about 200 milliseconds, no wait is longer than 30 seconds, and a call is tried at most six times.
Lengths of time, random numbers and the ledger’s errors.

out.says: A half-second pause between every try, with three tries at most. The growing, random wait replaces it.

src/bank/mod.rs.what: The ledger’s only way to the bank: it asks the bank to take a payment or give one back, each call with a key and a time limit.
src/bank/mod.rs.change: Calls to the bank had no key and no time limit. Now each carries the caller’s key and gives up after 15 seconds.

parts.says: Sends a payment with the caller’s key and a time limit, tried again by `with_retries`, so the bank takes it once however often it’s asked: [[Idempotency keys]].
parts.before: Sent the payment with no key and no time limit.

parts.says: Sends a refund the same way, with its own key, so a refund tried again is given once.
parts.before: Sent the refund with no key.

parts.says: One call may take 15 seconds; then it’s dropped, so the retry around it can start.
A client for the bank, from the settings: where the bank is, and the key to call it with.
The client, a payment as the bank takes it, and the receipt it sends back: approved or not, and why not.
Says what the file is for, and brings in time, settings, errors, amounts and retries.

src/api/v1/charges.rs.change: It used to charge every request it was sent. Now a request sent again with the same key gets the first receipt.

parts.says: Holds the money, asks the bank, then settles it or lets it go. A request whose key was answered before gets that receipt instead: [[Idempotency keys]].
parts.before: Charged every request it was sent, with no key.

parts.says: Looks up the receipt kept for a key, if a request with it was answered before.
Keeps the receipt under its key; a key kept already is left as it was.
What a shop sends to charge a card, and the receipt it gets back.

src/api/v1/refunds.rs.change: Refunds went to the bank with no key. Now the caller’s key goes with each one.

parts.says: Asks the bank to refund the payment with the caller’s key, then books the money from the merchant back to the customer: [[Idempotency keys]].
parts.before: Asked the bank with no key.

parts.says: What a shop sends to give a payment back, and the receipt it gets.

tests/retry.rs.what: Tests that each wait’s ceiling starts at 200 milliseconds, doubles with each try, and stops at 30 seconds.

parts.says: The ceiling is 200 milliseconds at first, 1.6 seconds by the fourth try, and never more than 30 seconds.
The same ceiling the retries work out: twice the last, up to the limit.

migrations/0002_request_keys.sql.what: Adds the table that remembers each request answered, so a request sent again isn’t charged twice.

parts.says: A table of the requests answered, by their key, with the receipt each got and when; a key can be in it only once: [[Unique keys]].
So a request sent again gets the same answer, not a second charge.

docs/retries.md.what: Explains how ledger retries its calls to the bank: which are tried again, how long each wait is, and why a retry never charges twice.
docs/retries.md.change: New: how retries work, for the people who run ledger.

parts.says: Calls that fail for reasons that pass are tried up to six times; one a retry can’t fix fails at once: [[Transient errors]].
The first wait is about 200 milliseconds, and each may double, up to 30 seconds, giving the bank room to recover: [[Exponential backoff]].
Each client picks a random time below the ceiling, so clients that failed together don’t return together: [[Jitter]].

parts.goal: Why a retry can’t charge twice
parts.says: Every payment carries a key the bank remembers, so a retry of one that went through changes nothing: [[Idempotency keys]].
A call that hangs gives up after 15 seconds, so the retry can start: [[Timeouts]].

src/reserve.rs.what: A charge in two steps: the customer’s money is held first, then taken once the bank agrees, or given back if it doesn’t.

parts.says: Moves the amount from the customer to held, one charge at a time for each customer, so two charges can’t both spend it: [[Advisory locks]].
Moves it from held to the merchant, once the bank says yes.
Moves it from held back to the customer, when the bank says no.

src/ledger.rs.what: The books: every movement of money is two entries that balance, written together or not at all.

parts.says: Takes an amount from one account and gives it to another, in one transaction, so the books always balance: [[Database transactions]].
Writes a debit and a credit of the same amount under one id, inside the transaction it’s given: [[Double-entry bookkeeping]].
Adds up an account’s entries in a currency. **It’s never stored, so it can never disagree with them.**
An amount in pence or cents, and a movement: from where, to where, how much, in what, and why.
